annotations.title: What past crises did to this mix

description:
What past crises did to one portfolio held as it is today: 2008, 2020, 2022 and the others
        inside its price history. In: holdings. Out: for each crisis the deepest fall, the
        worst day and the days until the previous high came back; crises before a holding
        existed are named as not tested. Typical questions: 'How much would 2008 have cost
        me with 60% VTI, 20% VXUS, 20% BND?'; 'What did the 2020 crash do to this mix?';
        'Simulate a market crash on my portfolio.'. Instead: for a loss chosen by the reader
        ('what would it take to lose 30%?'), reverse_stress. For the whole record,
        return_history. Holdings in money give each fall in money; in percentages the falls
        are percentages. It does not recommend, predict or calculate tax.

base.description: Currency code every figure is expressed in: USD, EUR, GBP, CAD… Default USD.
base.title: Base

holdings.description: What is held: {ticker: number}, 1 to 100 holdings. Weights in any scale (60/20/20 or 0.6/0.2/0.2) or money amounts in the base currency (60000/20000/20000): holdings adding up to 1 or 100 are read as percentages, anything else as money, which makes the falls come out in money. Tickers as the exchange lists them (VOO, VWCE.DE, EQQQ.DE, XAW.TO; 'CASH.USD' for cash). Example: {"VTI": 60, "VXUS": 20, "BND": 20}.
holdings.title: Holdings
